data_section_full_text:
3.1 Sample selection and data sources


ExecuComp provides information on the start and termination dates for CEOs,
which we supplement with hand-collected data. Using precise start and termination
dates enables us to identify instances of CEO turnover and compute CEO tenure on
123

CEO tenure and the performance-turnover relation


a quarterly basis. Monthly stock returns and fiscal quarter-end stock price data are
obtained from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) and quarterly
accounting data from the Compustat database.

Our sample spans 1996–2005. <sup>13</sup> For each sample firm, we collect quarterly
earnings and the consensus median analyst forecast immediately preceding the
quarterly earnings announcement date from the Institutional Brokers Estimate
System’s (I/B/E/S) unsplit-adjusted database. Our measures of monitoring intensity
are obtained from the Institutional Investors Research Center database, through
Institutional Shareholders Services (IRRC). <sup>14</sup>

Unlike most prior research on CEO turnover that uses annual data, we use
quarterly data in our empirical tests. This design choice allows us to more precisely
match CEO turnover and tenure to more precise measures of firm performance than
are available annually. CRSP, Compustat, and I/B/E/S data are available at the end
of each firm’s fiscal quarter. Thomson Financial 13F data, which is available on a
calendar quarter basis, is matched to the nearest firm fiscal quarter. ExecuComp and
IRRC data, which are available only annually, are matched to fiscal quarters by
taking fiscal year-end values for each variable and applying those to each fiscal
quarter in the year. Clearly, the lack of firm quarterly governance variables
introduces error in our measures, but we believe that this error is unlikely to be
systematically correlated with our variables of interest. Our final sample for the least
